pt.r: O Parque Nacional da Floresta Petrificada fica no Arizona, nos Estados Unidos. Tem 380 km² e está protegido desde 1962. Na classificação da IUCN, está na categoria II, a dos parques nacionais: protege ecossistemas inteiros e recebe visitantes.
pt.h: Povos indígenas viveram ali por mais de 13.000 anos e deixaram petróglifos e ruínas como Puerco Pueblo. Com o saque da madeira petrificada, virou monumento nacional em 1906 e parque nacional em 09/12/1962. A Route 66 cruzava a área.

en.r: Floresta Petrificada National Park is a national park in Arizona, United States. It covers 380 km² and has been protected since 1962. Under the IUCN system it is category II, the national park category: it protects whole ecosystems and welcomes visitors.
en.h: Indigenous peoples lived here for over 13,000 years, leaving petroglyphs and ruins such as Puerco Pueblo. Looting of petrified wood led to a national monument in 1906 and a national park on 9 December 1962. Route 66 crossed the area.
en.ff: Large deposits of Triassic petrified wood over 200 million years old, plus fossils of early reptiles and dinosaurs. To the north begin the colorful badlands of the Painted Desert.

pt.r: O Parque Nacional de Saguaro fica no Arizona, nos Estados Unidos. Tem 374 km² e está protegido desde 1994, sob gestão do Serviço Nacional de Parques dos EUA (NPS). Na classificação da IUCN, está na categoria II, a dos parques nacionais: protege ecossistemas inteiros e recebe visitantes.

pt.ff: Dois distritos, a leste e a oeste de Tucson, protegem o deserto de Sonora e o saguaro gigante, cacto que pode passar de 12 m e viver mais de 150 anos. Morcegos e aves polinizam as flores; há pecaris, coiotes, monstros-de-gila e corujas-elfas que fazem ninho nos cactos.

en.r: Saguaro National Park is a national park in Arizona, United States. It covers 374 km² and has been protected since 1994. It is managed by the U.S. National Park Service. Under the IUCN system it is category II, the national park category: it protects whole ecosystems and welcomes visitors.
en.h: The Tohono O'odham have harvested saguaro fruit for centuries. A national monument since 1933, it became a national park on 14 October 1994.
en.ff: Two districts east and west of Tucson protect the Sonoran Desert and the giant saguaro, a cactus that can top 12 m and live over 150 years. Bats and birds pollinate its flowers; there are javelinas, coyotes, Gila monsters and elf owls nesting in the cacti.

pt.r: O Chiricahua National Park é um parque nacional no Arizona, nos Estados Unidos. Está protegido desde 2026. Na classificação da IUCN, é uma paisagem protegida, onde natureza e uso humano tradicional convivem.

en.r: Chiricahua National Park is a national park in Arizona, United States. It has been protected since 2026. Under the IUCN system it is a protected landscape, where nature and traditional human use coexist.
en.h: Homeland of the Chiricahua Apache, of leaders such as Cochise and Geronimo. Created as a national monument on 18 April 1924 and redesignated the 64th US national park on 20 October 2026. It preserves Faraway Ranch, of Swedish immigrants Neil and Emma Erickson.
en.ff: It protects a maze of hoodoos and balancing rocks, columns of volcanic rock from a huge eruption 27 million years ago. The mountains are a "sky island" between deserts, rich in birds and plants; over 85% is wilderness.

en.r: Homolovi State Park is a state park in Arizona, United States. It covers 2 hectares and has been protected since 1986.
en.h: A park just north of Winslow, Arizona, protecting over 300 Ancestral Puebloan archaeological sites. Homol'ovi means 'place of the little hills' in Hopi; at the request of the Hopi, who see the sites as spiritually alive, 'Ruins' was dropped from the name in 2011. Seven pueblos were built around 1260-1400 on the Little Colorado floodplain.

en.r: Baboquivari Peak Wilderness is a wilderness area in Arizona, United States. It covers 8.3 km² and has been protected since 1990. It is managed by the Bureau of Land Management. Under the IUCN system it is a wilderness area: a large, largely unmodified space without permanent infrastructure.
en.h: A 2,065-acre (8 km2) wilderness in the Baboquivari Mountains, 50 miles (80 km) southwest of Tucson, Arizona, also called La Bestia, run by the Bureau of Land Management and co-stewarded by the Tohono O'odham Nation. Designated by Congress in 1990, it is Arizona's smallest wilderness. 7,730-foot (2,356 m) Baboquivari Peak is a technical summit popular with climbers and visible from Kitt Peak National Observatory. To the west lies the Tohono O'odham reservation, the second largest in the US.

en.r: Lost Dutchman State Park is a state park in Arizona, United States. It has been protected since 1977.
en.h: A 320-acre (129 ha) state park in northwestern Pinal County, Arizona, on the Apache Trail north of Apache Junction, near the Superstition Mountains, about 40 miles (64 km) east of Phoenix. en.r: Tonto Natural Bridge State Park is a state park in Arizona, United States.
en.h: A state park ten miles (16 km) north of Payson, Arizona, whose centerpiece is Tonto Natural Bridge, believed to be the largest natural travertine bridge in the world. The arch spans a 400-foot (120 m) tunnel up to 150 feet (46 m) wide and 183 feet (56 m) high. It was documented in 1877 by Scotsman David Gowan while hiding from Apaches; impressed, he brought his family to live there.

en.r: Saddle Mountain is a protected area in the United States. It has been protected since 1984.
en.h: A wilderness area in Kaibab National Forest, north of Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona, established in 1984. On the Kaibab Plateau, it includes Saddle Mountain, a saddle-shaped ridge reaching 2,568 m. Elevations rise from about 1,800 m at the edge of Marble Canyon to 2,400 m on the southern ridge, which forms the Grand Canyon's Nankoweap Rim.
en.ff: Pinyon pine and Utah juniper support mule deer in winter, which move up to the conifer forests in summer. A bison herd introduced in the early 20th century still roams the area.
at: Nankoweap Rim of the Grand Canyon

en.r: Arrastra Mountain Wilderness is a wilderness area in Arizona, United States. It covers 525 km² and has been protected since 1990. Under the IUCN system it is a wilderness area: a large, largely unmodified space without permanent infrastructure.
en.h: A wilderness area in Arizona established in 1990 under the Arizona Desert Wilderness Act and managed by the Bureau of Land Management. It centers on the Poachie Range, which rises to almost 1,500 m, and takes in more than 32 km of the ephemeral Big Sandy and Santa Maria rivers. West of the Big Sandy, the Artillery Mountains are dominated by Artillery Peak, a red volcanic plug 370 m tall.
en.ff: In Peoples Canyon, springs feed a 3.2 km chain of deep pools shaded by hundreds of sycamores, willows and cottonwoods.

es.h: Área silvestre en Arizona creada en 1990 por la Ley de Áreas Silvestres del Desierto de Arizona y gestionada por el Bureau of Land Management. Se centra en la sierra Poachie, que llega a casi 1.500 m, y abarca más de 32 km de los ríos intermitentes Big Sandy y Santa María. Al oeste del Big Sandy, los Artillery Mountains tienen como hito el Artillery Peak, un tapón volcánico rojo de 370 m de altura.
